meta.title: About — Pavlicevits Colors · Since 1990
meta.description: A family-run paint vendor in Kalamaria, Thessaloniki. Two generations on the counter. Specialist in architectural, automotive, marine, and special applications.

hero.lead: A family-run paint vendor with two generations working the counter. We began representing German paints in Northern Greece in 1982. We founded the current company in 1990. We expanded into automotive, marine, and special applications from 2002 onwards. Today the next generation drives the brand and digital work; the previous generation still runs the floor. The handoff is continuous, not sudden.

act1.title: Act 1
act1.body: We started as the Northern Greece representative for a German paint manufacturer. We learned that quality is a language: you either speak it or you don't.

act2.title: Act 2
act2.body: We founded the current company under our own name. The same family. The same standards. A wider remit.

act3.title: Act 3
act3.body: We expanded into the four specialty categories that define us today: architectural, automotive, marine, and special applications. We built the curation and the partnerships that make the shop what it is.

v1.title: The relationship is the product.
v1.body: The paint is the deliverable. The advice is the real service. The relationship is the actual product. Customers from 1995 still come to us. So do their kids.

v2.title: The right solution, not just the available one.
v2.body: Every recommendation we give is the one we'd use ourselves on our own job. Not the one with the highest margin. Not the one we want to clear from the back room.

v3.title: Material quality is non-negotiable.
v3.body: Pigment density. Resin chemistry. Lightfastness. Coverage. Adhesion. These are not abstract specs. They're the difference between a hotel facade that lasts seven years and one that lasts two.

v4.title: Color is transformation.
v4.body: A re-coated yacht hull is not a freshly painted yacht. It's a different vessel, ready for another five years at sea. We're in the business of transformation.

v5.title: We focus on the work, not the noise.
v5.body: Discipline is what gets the job right. Display is what gets the credit. We're more interested in the first.

shop.para1: The shop is staffed by people who answer to two generations of the same family. The previous generation defined the standards over decades of work. The next generation is bringing those standards into the present — into the digital, the new partnerships, the new ways of working.
shop.para2: The handoff has been continuous since the early 2000s. There's no transition month. No "the new owner takes over." Just two generations on the floor at the same time, working through the same jobs, holding to the same line.

hero.headlineLight: You don't pay for it. You earn it by walking in.
hero.lead: Walking in is the first step. We'll match the product to the job, the substrate to the system, the system to the conditions, and the conditions to your timeline and budget. The advice is part of what you came for.

architectural.title: Architectural advisory
architectural.body: Specialized counsel for interior and exterior systems — substrate diagnosis, moisture management, thermal considerations, coating strategy, color planning. From the spec to the application.

automotive.title: Automotive solutions
automotive.body: End-to-end support for body shops and individual restoration: paint, primers, clearcoats, polishing compounds, finishing tools. Color matching with calibrated equipment, not approximation.

marine.title: Marine applications
marine.body: Technical guidance for antifouling selection, primer compatibility, topcoat systems, and seasonal maintenance. We work with yards across Halkidiki, Sithonia, and the Thermaikos coastline.

industrial.title: Industrial and special
industrial.body: Solutions for floors, pools, metal structures, and the jobs that don't fit a catalog. Epoxy systems, chemical-resistant coatings, anti-slip treatments — specified to actual operating conditions.

colorMatch.title: Color matching study
colorMatch.body: Professional color matching with specialized equipment. We identify the exact hue from your sample — not the closest in our deck — and document it for repeatability across multi-phase jobs.

customColor.title: Custom color formulation
customColor.body: Bespoke color preparation per your specifications — from a sample, a photograph, or a unique idea. Done in the lab in Edessa with Pellachrom, with batch documentation for future re-orders.

tech.conditions: Year-round Sithonia exposure, salinity ≥ 3.5%, seasonal lay-up
tech.system: 2-pack epoxy primer + tie coat + 2-pack epoxy antifouling, 2 finish coats
tech.products: Pellachrom Marine — primer, tie coat, antifouling
tech.application: Two phases at yard, 7 days between phases

body.brief: The owner had previously seen 18-24 month service from a single-pack antifouling system on the same hull. The vessel sees year-round exposure at Porto Sani Marina with limited lay-up. The brief was straightforward: extend the maintenance interval without overspecifying.
body.spec: We specified a 2-pack epoxy system over a tie coat to manage adhesion across the existing primer. Pellachrom Marine was the right answer — both for performance under salinity and for the practical proximity (we coordinated the application window with the yard and the manufacturer's technical desk).
body.application: Phase one in mid-March, with primer and tie coat. Phase two seven days later, with the antifouling and finish. The yard handled the application; we handled the spec, the materials, and the on-call technical questions.
body.result: The owner contacted us this season for the first re-inspection — six years on. Adhesion intact. Color stable. No biofouling beyond cosmetic. Re-coat is due in approximately 12-18 months.

meta.title: Partnerships — Pellachrom + Curated Brands · Pavlicevits Colors
meta.description: Official Pellachrom partner. Plus Vivechrom, Vechro, Kraft, Vitex, and Isomat — curated, not warehoused. Each brand earns its place on our shelves.

hero.lead: We don't carry every brand. We carry the ones we've tested, used on our own work, and would recommend without hesitation. Each one is here for a specific reason.

pellachrom.para1: D.G.K. Pellachrom has been making paint in Edessa, in the Pella regional unit of Northern Greece, since 1981. Our cooperation with them is a working relationship — direct, technical, and ongoing.
pellachrom.para2: What "official partnership" means in practice: when we specify a Pellachrom system for a customer project, we have direct lines to the formulators if a substrate or exposure question comes up. When a project needs a custom batch — non-standard hue, modified resin, special pigment ratio for repeatability across phases — we can request it. The supply chain is short: Edessa to Kalamaria is roughly 100 km. Stock is fresh. Custom-batch turnaround is a phone call.
pellachrom.para3: Pellachrom's range covers marine, decorative, anti-corrosion, industrial, and eco lines. Where their product is the right answer, we recommend it. Where it isn't — and we are honest about this — we recommend something else from our other partners.
pellachrom.para4: The relationship matters because it lets us specify, not just sell. A generic distribution arrangement tells you what's on the catalog. A working partnership lets us specify systems for the actual job in front of us.

vivechrom.name: Vivechrom
vivechrom.subtitle: AkzoNobel — Greek market leader since 1964
vivechrom.body: Vivechrom holds the leading position in the Greek architectural paint market. The breadth of their decorative range, the depth of their technical documentation, and their professional acceptance across the industry make them a default for many architectural specifications.

vechro.name: Vechro
vechro.subtitle: Greek-owned, 70+ years, eco-paint leader
vechro.body: Vechro is the Greek company most committed to ecological paint: 96 certified eco products. For projects where independent eco-certification is required (LEED, BREEAM, internal corporate ESG), Vechro is often the right specification.

kraft.name: Kraft Paints
kraft.subtitle: Druckfarben group — 900+ sales points nationally
kraft.body: For value-tier work where the price-quality balance must be precise, Kraft is reliable. The product range is wide. The performance is consistent. We use them for jobs that don't justify higher specifications — and we say so plainly.

vitex.name: Vitex
vitex.subtitle: Greek decorative
vitex.body: Where Vitex's specific lines outperform alternatives, we stock them. Some of their decorative interiors are best-in-category; we carry those.

isomat.name: Isomat
isomat.subtitle: Construction chemicals
isomat.body: For projects that cross the line between paint and construction chemistry — sealants, adhesives, restoration mortars — Isomat provides reliable specifications. We coordinate with them on integrated jobs.

curation.headlineLight: Every product passes them, or it isn't on our shelves.
curation.intro: When we evaluate whether a product earns shelf space, we apply six tests in this order:

t1.title: Performance under real conditions
t1.body: Not lab spec sheets. We use it ourselves or watch trusted painters use it.

t2.title: Pigment integrity over time
t2.body: Does the color hold at year five, or fade by year two?

t3.title: Coverage and yield
t3.body: Does the listed yield match field reality?

t4.title: Substrate compatibility
t4.body: Does it adhere properly across the substrates our customers actually face?

t5.title: Documented technical support
t5.body: Datasheets, MSDS, manufacturer responsiveness when there's a question.

curation.outro: If a product fails any of these in our experience, it leaves the shelf.

single.ctaTitle: Have a marine job we should look at?

body.lead: Northern Greek waters — from Sithonia to the Thermaikos — have their own identity. Salinity around 3.5%, big temperature swings, springtime biological activity that explodes within weeks. Antifouling isn't a consumable. It's a system.
body.p1Title: First test: what your hull can take
body.p1: Before we choose antifouling, we read the hull. New GRP? Polyester with a repaint history? Aluminum with galvanic protection? Every substrate has its own scenario. Adhesion, expansion, reaction with old primers. There is no one answer that covers all of them.
body.p2: Year-round in the water? Seasonal? Out for the winter? The application window changes completely. A boat that goes in at Easter and comes out in November doesn't need what a working vessel in continuous service does. We specify for your conditions, not the Aegean average.
body.p3: Antifouling is one link in a chain. Primer, tie coat, antifouling, finish coats. One weak link and the chain snaps at 18 months. The whole conversation is about color, but often the life of the system is decided in the tie coat — exactly where few people look.
body.outro: These three tests are how every marine conversation in our shop begins. Bring us the boat, the conditions, the history. We'll specify the continuity.
